name: forkcost
description: The shell's fork-then-exec hot path costs exactly two user-image copies (apple/fgx#494): the fork snapshot and the restore.  The kernel counts every copy in _kImgCopies; the poison zeroes it at the paste frame, after boot's own forks, and forkcost_check.py reads it after `/bin/true` completes.  A child that released its parent on an uninterruptible sleep (exec's disk reads) would swap the parent in and raise the count.  The poke's bank byte is the core kernel bank, $7C (the kimg region reads $7C96D3; FGX_DATA, which allocwarm pokes, is the next bank up).  A poke that missed leaves the boot's whole count (70 when this was written), which fails rather than passes.
